recipes.name: Tuyen Quang Tay cone-shaped sticky rice cake
recipes.description: A traditional Tay cone-shaped sticky rice cake wrapped in green leaves with black beans. Bếp Việt adapts the soaking, wrapping and simmering method for a small home batch so the rice cooks tender and fragrant.
recipes.serving_basis: 6 cone-shaped sticky rice cakes with black beans, served with sesame salt.
recipes.finished_dish: Neat cone-shaped cakes have tender, glossy sticky rice around nutty black beans, with a gentle leaf aroma; serve warm with sesame salt.
recipes.serving: Let the cakes drain briefly, then unwrap while warm. Serve with sesame salt or lightly crushed peanut salt.
tips: Soak the sticky rice and black beans separately so they soften evenly before wrapping.
Tie the leaves firmly enough to hold their shape while leaving room for the rice to expand.
Keep the cakes covered with water at a gentle boil; larger cakes may need extra time.
recipes.image_alt: Tuyen Quang Tay cone-shaped sticky rice cakes wrapped in leaves and filled with black beans.
recipes.time_note: Boiling time depends on cake size and rice variety; test one cake before turning off the heat.
search_terms: Tuyen Quang Tay sticky rice cake
cone-shaped sticky rice with black beans
ingredients: Rinse, soak separately for 2–3 hours, then drain.
Sort, soak for 2–3 hours and drain.
Wipe clean and briefly blanch to soften; use two layers per cake.
Season the rice; reserve a little for the cooking water if needed.
preparation_steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak for 2 hours. Soak the black beans separately for the same time; drain both.
Wash and wipe the leaves, then blanch briefly to soften. Prepare the bamboo ties and mix the rice with salt.
cooking_steps: Mix the soaked rice and black beans. Shape leaves into cones, fill with the mixture and press firmly so cooking water cannot seep inside. Fold into a cone and tie with bamboo strips.
Place cakes in a pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 2 to 2½ hours, topping up with hot water to keep them submerged.
Drain the cakes and rest for 5 minutes. Serve warm with sesame or peanut salt.

recipes.name: Crispy battered Mekong flood-season fish
recipes.description: A Mekong Delta seasonal fish dish: small cá linh are coated in a light egg batter and fried golden. Bếp Việt adapts the home method and pairs the crisp fish with fresh garden greens.
recipes.serving_basis: 4 portions of crisp battered fish with fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.
recipes.finished_dish: Palm-sized golden cá linh fritters with a delicate crisp coating and tender, fragrant fish, served with fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.
recipes.serving: Serve immediately while crisp. Wrap with young mustard greens, lettuce and herbs, then dip in sweet-sour fish sauce.
tips: Choose fresh small fish, rinse gently and dry thoroughly so the batter adheres evenly.
Use just enough batter to coat the fish; the mixture should not be runny.
Fry in small batches at moderate heat and drain on a rack to preserve crispness.
recipes.image_alt: Palm-sized Mekong cá linh fritters coated in light egg batter and fried golden, served with fresh greens.
recipes.time_note: Small fish cook quickly; frying time varies with fish size and oil temperature. Make sure the fish is cooked through.
ingredients: Choose fresh fish; remove gills if desired, rinse gently and drain.
Sift; part may be replaced with rice flour for a lighter crisp coating.
Add gradually until the batter is lightly thick.
Amount depends on the frying pot.
Young mustard greens, lettuce and herbs
Wash and drain for wrapping the fish.
preparation_steps: Clean the fish, remove gills if desired, rinse gently in lightly salted water, rinse quickly and dry thoroughly.
Whisk flour, egg yolk, water, salt and pepper until lightly thick. Wash and drain the greens and prepare sweet-sour fish sauce.
cooking_steps: Toss the fish in just enough batter for a thin coating. Heat oil over medium heat; a drop of batter should rise steadily.
Add a portion of fish and batter, press it flat into a palm-sized fritter and fry until deep golden and crisp, turning as needed. Drain on a rack or paper.
Serve hot with fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce. Do not cover while hot, as trapped steam softens the coating.

recipes.name: Mixed garden greens soup with shrimp
recipes.description: A light Vietnamese home-style soup combining seasonal garden greens with fresh shrimp for a gently sweet, clear broth. Bếp Việt adapts the order of adding greens so each variety stays tender and green.
recipes.serving_basis: 4 bowls of seasonal garden greens soup with fresh shrimp.
recipes.finished_dish: A gently sweet shrimp broth with tender green leaves and pink shrimp, served hot and fresh.
recipes.serving: Ladle into bowls and serve hot with steamed rice and a mild savory dish. Eat promptly so the greens keep their color and freshness.
tips: Combine three to five tender leafy greens; trim tough parts and wash thoroughly.
Pound or chop the shrimp coarsely so the broth is flavorful while small shrimp pieces remain.
Add firmer greens first and tender leaves last; cook only until just done.
recipes.image_alt: Vietnamese mixed garden greens soup with pink shrimp in a clear, gently sweet broth.
recipes.time_note: Add the greens to a briskly boiling broth and cook for no more than 3 minutes in total to preserve their color.
ingredients: Peel and devein, then pound coarsely with half the salt.
Combine purslane, water spinach, amaranth, Malabar spinach, gotu kola or other available leaves.
Use half to pound the shrimp and the rest to season after cooking.
For frying the shallot and shrimp.
preparation_steps: Peel and devein the shrimp, then pound or chop coarsely with salt. Pick through the greens, wash thoroughly and drain.
Cut tough stems into small pieces and separate them from tender leaves. Chop the shallot.
cooking_steps: Pound the shrimp coarsely with half the salt. Fry the shallot in oil, add the shrimp and cook for about 1 minute until pink-orange.

Pour 1 litre of water into the pot, bring to a boil, lower the heat and skim for a clear broth. Once boiling briskly, add purslane and gotu kola first; after about 1 minute add amaranth and water spinach, then Malabar spinach and chives last.
Keep the total cooking time for the greens to 3 minutes or less. Turn off the heat, season with the remaining salt and add pepper; leave the pot uncovered while hot.
keywords: Mixed garden greens soup with shrimp

recipes.name: Ben Tre hand-cut rice noodle and duck soup
recipes.description: A rustic Ben Tre noodle soup made by rolling rice dough and cutting the strands directly into a simmering duck broth. Bếp Việt adapts the home method for tender noodles, a gently cloudy broth and fragrant ginger.
recipes.serving_basis: 5 bowls of hand-cut rice noodles with tender duck in ginger broth.
recipes.finished_dish: Soft, lightly chewy rice noodles sit in fragrant ginger duck broth with tender meat; serve with a small dish of ginger fish sauce.
recipes.serving: Ladle noodles and broth into bowls, top with duck, scallions, herbs and pepper. Serve ginger fish sauce on the side for dipping the meat.
tips: Knead until the dough is smooth, pliable and no longer sticky; add water gradually.
Roll and cut the noodles directly over gently simmering broth to prevent them sticking together.
After adding the dough, avoid a hard boil because starch can settle on the bottom of the pot.
recipes.image_alt: Ben Tre hand-cut rice noodles and tender duck served in a gently cloudy ginger broth.
recipes.time_note: Flour absorbs water differently; adjust the dough until pliable, not wet. Cut strands into gently simmering broth.
search_terms: Ben Tre banh canh bot xat
ingredients: Cut into serving pieces; trim excess fat for a lighter broth.
Fine plain rice flour for rolling and cutting the noodles.
Adds a little chew to the noodles.
Divide between the broth and ginger dipping sauce.
Crush and simmer with the duck.
Cover the duck and make the broth.
Divide between the broth and ginger dipping sauce.
preparation_steps: Rub the duck with salt and ginger, rinse clean and cut into pieces. Roast or pan-char some ginger until fragrant, then crush it.
Combine rice flour, tapioca starch and salt. Gradually add warm water and knead until smooth and pliable; cover and rest for 20 minutes.
cooking_steps: Add duck, ginger, shallot and water to a pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer until tender, about 35–45 minutes.
Remove the duck to cool slightly. Roll the dough about 3 mm thick, dust lightly with flour and cut into 5–7 mm strands.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer. Add noodles a little at a time, stirring gently along the bottom. Cook until they float and turn opaque; season with fish sauce and salt.
Return the duck to the pot to warm through. Serve the noodles with scallions, herbs, pepper and ginger fish sauce.

recipes.name: Hue turmeric rice vermicelli stir-fry
recipes.description: A humble Hue noodle dish combining rice vermicelli with golden turmeric, thoroughly cleaned pork offal, onion and Vietnamese coriander. Bếp Việt adapts the preparation to cook the offal fully and stir-fry the noodles briefly so they stay separate.
recipes.serving_basis: 4 portions of turmeric rice vermicelli stir-fried with pork offal and herbs.
recipes.finished_dish: Loose golden turmeric noodles with fully cooked pork offal, scallions and aromatic Vietnamese coriander.
recipes.serving: Serve hot with Vietnamese coriander, scallions and pepper. Add fresh chilli and a squeeze of lime to taste.
tips: Clean and boil the offal until fully cooked; do not serve it raw or undercooked.
If using dried vermicelli, soak and blanch according to the package, then drain before stir-frying.
Cook the turmeric over medium heat and toss the noodles briefly so they do not break apart.
recipes.image_alt: Hue turmeric rice vermicelli stir-fried with fully cooked pork offal, scallions and Vietnamese coriander.
recipes.time_note: Boiling time depends on the type and size of offal; always cook it fully before stir-frying.
ingredients: Gently separate; briefly blanch and drain if chilled.
Wash thoroughly, boil until fully cooked, then slice.
Peel and pound; wear gloves to avoid staining.
Slice, separating white and green parts.
preparation_steps: Wash the offal several times with salt and ginger or vinegar, then rinse. Boil in water until fully cooked; drain, cool and slice.
Gently separate the vermicelli. Pound the turmeric, chop the garlic, slice the shallot and wash the herbs and scallions.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the shallot, garlic and white scallion until fragrant. Add turmeric and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked offal and season with fish sauce, salt and pepper. Add vermicelli in batches and toss gently until evenly golden and hot.
Turn off the heat and fold in Vietnamese coriander and scallions. Serve hot with pepper and fresh chilli if desired.
